goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/apim.json (47 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Access control (IAM), Tags, Diagnose and solve problems, Events, APIs, Developer portal, Monitoring, Deployment + infrastructure, Security, Settings, Automation, Help)
Backend: ARM Microsoft.ApiManagement service, APIs, operations, products as config
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/apim.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.apim.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape

depth_targets.title: Protocol settings / Protocols + ciphers (properties.customProperties)
limitations: TLS/SSL protocol and cipher flags round-trip through ARM exactly as configured, but Vyomi's gateway never negotiates TLS, so disabling a protocol here has no effect on anything.

depth_targets.title: Creating an API from WebSocket, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI, WSDL, WADL, or an Azure resource (API App / Function App / Container App / Logic App); restricting a new API to specific gateways
limitations: Only the HTTP creation flow (display name, name, web service URL, API URL suffix, description, URL scheme, product) is modeled. Every other creation source, and per-API gateway restriction, is not simulated — new APIs are always reachable on the managed gateway.

depth_targets.title: Named values of type Key Vault
limitations: The Key Vault secret identifier round-trips through ARM exactly as configured, but Vyomi never resolves it against a live Key Vault secret — matching the real portal, which also never displays the resolved value in this grid.

depth_targets.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the timespan picker are not modeled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

depth_targets.title: Access control (IAM) on a service
limitations: Role assignments scoped to an individual resource are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Developer portal (overview, settings, Users, Groups, Identities, Delegation)
limitations: The developer portal CMS, its user/group/identity-provider directory, and delegation are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Application Insights, Alerts, Metrics, Diagnostic settings, Logs, Analytics
limitations: Metrics charts, alert rules, diagnostic-setting log routing, Log Analytics queries and API analytics are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Network, Custom domains, Locations, Scale out and up, Pricing tier (post-creation), Managed identities (user-assigned), Certificates, Gateways, Self-hosted gateways, Defender for Cloud
limitations: Multi-region deployment, VNet/custom-domain/certificate configuration, scale units, managed/self-hosted gateways and Defender for Cloud are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Events, MCP Servers, API Tags, Policy fragments, Workspaces, Credential manager, Tasks, Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: These portal troubleshooting, catalog and support tools are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Export template
limitations: The ARM Template tab is generated from the live resource; Bicep and Terraform export are not modeled.

note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.
